newsitem.title: USA: Folgers says no retail coffee price hike.
newsitem.headline: Folgers says no retail coffee price hike.

text.p: Procter and Gamble Co unit Folgers Coffee Co said Thursday that, contrary to rumors, it has not raised the price of its retail coffee.
"They can talk about rumors all they want," a spokeswoman for Folgers said. "We do not have any news."
Traders on the floor of Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) in New York said talk of a price hike at Folgers helped drive futures prices to new contract highs Thursday.

While no U.S. coffee roaster has raised its posted prices yet, analysts say increases may not be far off if the recent uptrend in the futures market continues. Since the beginning of the year, prices have surged by nearly 30 percent.
But, analysts added, roasters were likely to wait for futures volatility to subside.
"The roasters will be cautious," one coffee analyst said. "They will have to let the market stabilize for at least a few weeks."
Last month, Procter and Gamble's Canadian division announced a price rise of Folgers coffee in Canada effective on Feb. 1 to reflect gains in green bean prices.

"Our intention is to reflect North American green bean prices," a spokeswoman for Proctor's Canadian unit said at the time. "We last lowered the price on Aug. 1, and that was to be in line with competitive pricing."

At 1327 EST, benchmark March coffee futures were up 6.05 cents at 150.60 cents a lb, just off a new life-of-contract high of 150.80 cents set earlier. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
